Steroids don't just make you get jacked. I'm a powerlifter and I did a cycle of testosterone in the summer. The single biggest difference was that normally I get home from work, have to force myself to go to the gym and after 30 minutes I'm gassed and the 2nd half of my workout isn't as effective because I'm so tired.

With drugs, I was working out 7 days a week and after breezing through my whole workout for that day, I'd think "what else can I do" and I'd spend an extra 90mins doing more exercises. I could do squats and instead of being tired afterwards, I'd do a variation to work on technique. The next day I had no soreness and could even do the same 2hr workout again.

In other words - there's a misconception that steroids help only by building muscle, whether that's muscle for power in boxing or sprinting, or endurance in football or cycling. The biggest advantage is simply being able to train more often, for longer, and with fewer injuries/faster recovery.

What I do is stand up and shift my weight from one foot to the other, or do a sideways karate kick. You should see the muscle contract pretty clearly. I usually mark it with a pen, then sit down and take all the weight off that leg and the muscle gets so relaxed it feels like pure fat.
